<thought>Based on the spectrum, a strong M+1 peak (~16 % of the base) indicates many carbon atoms, but carbon’s isotopic pattern isn’t unique enough to be “definitively identified.” The presence of two distinct peaks at nominal mass 237 (separated by ~0.01 Da) alongside a clear M+2 peak at 236 (≈16 % of the base) matches the characteristic 35Cl/37Cl pattern (≈3:1, giving an M+2 peak ~33 % of the monoisotopic intensity). The observed M+2 intensity (~16 %) is lower than the ideal 33 % because the ion also contains many carbons, diluting the relative chlorine contribution, yet the distinct 2‑Da spacing and the known chlorine isotopic ratio allow us to definitively identify chlorine. No comparable 1:1 M+2 pattern (indicative of bromine) or the smaller M+2 (~4 %) pattern of sulfur is evident. Therefore, the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution is chlorine. 

The answer should be a list of element symbols.
